notes.chunk_at_written: … What he built in 1888 was a customer who had never existed: an ordinary person, with no chemistry and no darkroom, who could keep a piece of their own life. *You press the button, we do the rest.* It was the first true consumer company in America, and the promise was so complete that the man behind it disappeared into it. He removed himself from the product, from his gifts, from his own authorized biography, and finally from the world, on a March afternoon in 1932, with the alternative covered and a second pistol in the bookcase. The company he left ran on his instructions for eighty years without the judgment that wrote them. It gave the United States its eyes over the Soviet Union, put the first photograph of the Earth in front of humanity, and then, in a single year, 1976, invented the digital image, patented the sensor every phone now carries, licensed it out to the world, and chose to collect rent instead of build. …
notes.stood_on: He removed himself from the product, from his gifts, from his own authorized biography, and finally from the world, on a March afternoon in 1932, with the alternative covered and a second pistol in the bookcase.
notes.answered_by: He arrived at most of it before the men history remembers for it.
notes.verdict: Survived as the essay's credit motif; the Ford claim died

notes.text: what did he see in MIT?
notes.chunk_at_written: He gave away the bulk of a fortune while he was alive rather than leaving a foundation behind him, and much of it anonymously. In 1912, with MIT financially strapped and Harvard maneuvering to absorb it, he gave the institute two and a half million dollars under the name Mr. Smith. The money built the new Cambridge campus and left MIT solvent enough to refuse Harvard's terms. He kept the secret for eight years. That same year he bought a company in London in order to acquire one scientist, and told him his job was the future of photography. That laboratory produced Kodachrome, and color is what turned a photograph from a record into a memory.
notes.stood_on: That same year he bought a company in London in order to acquire one scientist, and told him his job was the future of photography.
notes.answered_by: Twenty-five years later, on the evening of March 5, 1912, he sat down at the Hotel Belmont in New York with the president of MIT.
notes.verdict: Survived verbatim: the essay's only blockquote
notes.why: 22:05 from Ackerman: Eastman to Maclaurin, 'no other place where a large sum of money could be invested with more effectiveness'; MIT as Kodak's hiring ground; v3 (22:10) makes MIT the third scene
